Title: Fetal auditory evoked responses to onset of amplitude modulated sounds. A fetal magnetoencephalography (fMEG) study.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: fetuses at 31 to 40 weeks of gestation (55 pregnant women)
Stimulus_Type: amplitude modulated tone (500 Hz carrier) presented to maternal abdomen
Outcome: Response latencies decreased for middle/high modulation rates vs low; maturation effect observed for 4/s only
Evidence_Quote: Fetal MEG was recorded during the presentation of an amplitude modulated tone (AM) with a carrier frequency of 500 Hz to the maternal abdomen modulated by low modulation rates (MRs) - 2/s and 4/s, middle MR - 8/s and high MRs - 27/s, 42/s, 78/s and 91/s.

Title: Unlike Kangaroo care, mechanically simulated Kangaroo care does not change heart rate variability in preterm neonates.
Journal: Early human development
Stimulus_Type: Kangaroo care; simulated Kangaroo care; heartbeat sounds
Evidence_Quote: To investigate whether a mattress that aims to mimic breathing motion and the sounds of heartbeats (BabyBe GMBH, Stuttgart, Germany) can simulate aspects of KC in preterm infants as measured by features of heart rate variability (HRV).

Title: Prosody-driven syntax learning is robust to impoverished pitch and spectral cues.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: syntax learning; prosodic bootstrapping; detection of prosodic boundaries
Evidence_Quote: In two artificial grammar experiments, adult native English speakers showed a similar ability to use English-like prosody to bootstrap unfamiliar syntactic structures from degraded speech and natural, unmanipulated speech.

Title: An age-dependent vocal tract model for males and females based on anatomic measurements.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infancy to 12 yrs, as well as adults
Evidence_Quote: The resulting model was assessed qualitatively by projecting hypothetical vocal tract shapes onto midsagittal images from the cohort of children, and quantitatively by comparison of formant frequencies produced by the model to those reported in the literature.

Title: Watch and listen - A cross-cultural study of audio-visual-matching behavior in 4.5-month-old infants in German and Swedish talking faces.
Journal: Infant behavior & development
Stimulus_Type: audio-visual speech; German and Swedish speech
Outcome: looking times; eye gaze; audio-visual matching
Evidence_Quote: The present study aimed to address this issue by tracking the eye gaze of 4.5-month-old German and Swedish infants cross-culturally in an intersensory matching procedure, comparing German and Swedish, two same-rhythm-class languages differing in phonetic and phonological attributes but not in prosody.

Title: Effects of consonantal context on the learnability of vowel categories from infant-directed speech.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Outcome: vowel categorization; learning of vowel categories
Evidence_Quote: The current study investigates whether vowel variability is partially due to consonantal context, and explores whether consonantal context could support the learning of vowel categories from IDS.

Title: Music reduces pain perception in healthy newborns: A comparison between different music tracks and recoded heartbeat.
Journal: Early human development
Target_Age: 80 healthy full-term newborns aged 1 to 3 days
Stimulus_Type: music tracks (Mozart, Beethoven) and heartbeat sound recordings
Outcome: Music/heartbeat groups showed reduced heart rate and pain perception and increased oxygen saturation vs control
Evidence_Quote: Prospective study of 80 full-term newborns, aged 1 to 3 days, randomly allocated to exposure to Mozart's Sonata for two pianos K.448, Beethoven's Moonlight Sonata, heartbeat sound recordings (70 bpm) or no music.

Title: Infants' sensitivity to rhyme in songs.
Journal: Infant behavior & development
Evidence_Quote: Novel children's songs with rhyming and non-rhyming lyrics using pseudo-words were presented to 35 9-month-old Dutch infants using the Headturn Preference Procedure.

Title: Typologies of dyadic mother-infant emotion regulation following immunization.
Journal: Infant behavior & development
Outcome: infant crying; maternal soothing behaviors; dyadic emotion regulation
Evidence_Quote: Mother-infant dyads (N = 131) were videotaped during a routine immunization procedure, and infant crying and maternal soothing behaviors were subsequently coded.

Title: Infants use onset asynchrony cues in auditory scene analysis.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Evidence_Quote: The ability to identify the target vowel was compared among three conditions: synchronous onset, 100-, and 200-ms onset asynchrony.

Title: The effect of noise exposure during the developmental period on the function of the auditory system.
Journal: Hearing research
Evidence_Quote: This paper reviews the effects of early interventions to the auditory system, in particular, of sound exposure during ontogeny.

Title: Infant pitch perception: Missing fundamental melody discrimination.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Evidence_Quote: This study investigated whether 3-month-olds, 7-month-olds, and adults can detect a change in a melody composed of missing fundamental complexes.

Title: Effect of the relationship between target and masker sex on infants' recognition of speech.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Evidence_Quote: So when do infants begin to use talker-gender cues for stream segregation? These studies find that 16-month-olds do not show an advantage when the masker and target differ in sex.

Title: Characterizing spontaneous otoacoustic emissions across the human lifespan.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: 632 human subjects, premature birth through seventh decade of life
Stimulus_Type: spontaneous otoacoustic emissions (SOAEs); no presented stimulus
Outcome: Newborn SOAEs an average of 5 to 6 dB higher in level, higher-frequency and more numerous than in young adults
Evidence_Quote: Newborn SOAEs are also an average of 5 to 6 dB higher in level than those from young-adult ears.

Title: Infants adapt to speaking rate differences in word segmentation.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Stimulus_Type: speech passages at varying speaking rates
Evidence_Quote: The results indicate that 14-month-olds, but not 11-month-olds, recognized target words in passages with a fast speaking rate.

Title: Directional asymmetries reveal a universal bias in adult vowel perception.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Evidence_Quote: In subsequent AX discrimination tests, both Canadian-English and Canadian-French listeners performed better at discriminating changes from less to more focal /u/'s compared to the reverse, regardless of variation in prototypicality.

Title: Is sensory processing an issue for infants with colic?
Journal: Infant behavior & development
Target_Age: infants with colic younger than 4 months of age
Outcome: sensory functioning; sleep; cry/fuss; feeding behaviors
Evidence_Quote: To determine the association between sensory functioning, sleep, cry/fuss, and feeding behaviors of infants with colic younger than 4 months of age.

Title: Prosodic exaggeration within infant-directed speech: Consequences for vowel learnability.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Evidence_Quote: Categorization models trained on prosodically exaggerated tokens outperformed models that were trained on tokens that were not exaggerated.

Title: Research Priorities in Sudden Unexpected Infant Death: An International Consensus.
Journal: Pediatrics
Evidence_Quote: The Global Action and Prioritization of Sudden Infant Death Project was an international consensus process that aimed to define and direct future research by investigating the priorities of expert and lay members of the sudden unexpected infant death (SUID) community across countries.

Title: The MMN as a viable and objective marker of auditory development in CI users.
Journal: Hearing research
Target_Age: infants and small children with CI
Evidence_Quote: In infants and small children with CI, the MMN provides the only means for assessing the adequacy of the CI functioning, its improvement as a function of time of CI use, and the efficiency of different rehabilitation procedures.

Title: Input matters: Multi-accent language exposure affects word form recognition in infancy.
Journal: The Journal of the Acoustical Society of America
Target_Age: infants prior to the emergence of phonological constancy (∼18 months)
Evidence_Quote: This study demonstrates that daily exposure to multiple accents strongly impacts infants' performance in a laboratory word form recognition task.
